Use the CLI from this Apporo Assistant source checkout (tools/mika/scripts/mika_cli.py). Set MIKA_ANDROID_PACKAGE=com.apporo.assistant before connecting over authorized USB ADB. For Wi-Fi or a private VPN, use the address shown on the phone and a private token file. Run connect or doctor to verify connectivity. Do not submit tasks or print tokens. See docs-apporo/agent-quickstart.en.md in the source checkout.

Add a Streamable HTTP MCP server at http://127.0.0.1:%1$d/mcp. Use the connection token from Apporo Assistant as a Bearer Authorization header, stored privately. Never print it in the conversation. Refresh the tools and check the request time on the phone. See docs-apporo/mcp.en.md in the source checkout.

After Wi-Fi drops or the phone restarts, the system turns “Wireless debugging” off. Phone control normally doesn’t need it — only when restarting (for example after an Apporo Assistant update). With this on, in those moments and while on Wi-Fi, Apporo Assistant turns it on and reconnects, but never turns it off for you. This uses the same “Modify system settings” permission as “Restore after restart” and works only on Wi-Fi you’ve allowed. Turn it off and Apporo Assistant stops doing this.

Phone control has stopped. This can happen after an Apporo Assistant update or a phone restart. Open Apporo Assistant, connect the phone to your computer, and rerun the current USB start command from “Set up phone control”. Confirm that Phone control shows Ready before retrying. Web and file tasks are not affected.

The USB helper cannot restart itself after an Apporo Assistant update or a phone restart. Open Apporo Assistant, connect to your computer, and rerun the current USB start command in “Set up phone control”. Continue when Phone control shows Ready.
Connect the phone to a computer with USB and run this command on the computer. After an Apporo Assistant update or a phone restart, open Apporo Assistant and run the current command again.

Connect the phone to a computer with USB and run the command shown here. On most phones the helper keeps running after unplugging. If it stops, or after an Apporo Assistant update or phone restart, open Apporo Assistant and run the current command again. Check that Phone control shows Ready.

Keep USB debugging on. The helper was started with the USB command. On most phones it keeps running after unplugging. After an Apporo Assistant update or a phone restart, open Apporo Assistant and run the current USB start command again; confirm that Phone control shows Ready.

The helper was started with the USB command. Keep USB debugging on. On most phones it keeps running after unplugging; some systems stop it. After an Apporo Assistant update, a phone restart, or a stopped helper, open Apporo Assistant, connect to your computer, and rerun the current command from “Set up phone control”. Check that Phone control shows Ready. If Wireless debugging works on this phone, pairing allows automatic reconnection.
